tldr: Consolidated EBITDA reached an all-time high of Rs. 62,409 Cr, up 24% YoY, driven by strong O2C performance and Jio growth.
O2C segment delivered record EBITDA of Rs. 25,203 Cr (+69% YoY) benefiting from tight energy markets and operational flexibility.
Jio Platforms reported 18% higher EBITDA at Rs. 22,200 Cr with 542 million subscribers and 300 million 5G users.
Retail EBITDA margin at 7.8% reflects a conscious strategy to invest in digital commerce infrastructure, with grocery online revenue up 42% YoY.
New Energy complex remains on track for revenue contribution starting in FY 2028.
management_commentary: O2C performance validated by structural supply issues and operational excellence in crude sourcing despite elevated OpEx and freight costs.
Jio Platforms sees visibility of high teen growth driven by customer base expansion and digital service layering.
Retail strategy remains focused on long-term digital commerce scale, trading off short-term earnings for future value creation in FY 2028-29.
FMCG business achieved 1.6x YoY revenue growth in Q2, with focus on manufacturing and distribution expansion.
JioStar digital business reached 440 million MAU, with monetization improving through the quarter.
guidance: H1 FY 2027 performance tracking toward annualized EBITDA well over Rs. 80,000 Cr for O2C.
New Energy earnings contribution expected to start in FY 2028.
Retail business expects margin accretion and benefits of scale to reflect in absolute EBITDA from next year.
BESS facility commissioning expected in next calendar half-year, with cell production ramping up late next year.

segment_performance.notes: EBITDA up 69% YoY to Rs. 25,203 Cr; benefited from tight fuel markets and flexible crude sourcing from Americas/Med regions.
Revenue Rs. 40,475 Cr (+11.4% YoY); EBITDA Rs. 21,879 Cr (+16.6% YoY); 5G subscriber base reached 300 million.
Revenue grew 6.4% YoY; EBITDA Rs. 6,228 Cr; online grocery revenue up 42% YoY; 303 new stores opened.
Revenue Rs. 8,266 Cr (1.6x YoY); beverages led by Campa delivered Rs. 5,250 Cr in H1.
Steady quarter with KG-D6 production sustained at 25 million standard cubic meters; natural decline offset by elevated prices.

notable_qa.question: Probal Sen (ICICI Securities) asked about the timeline for normalization of the 5 million barrels/day of impacted refining capacity.
notable_qa.answer: Management noted high uncertainty and that normalization is not expected immediately given ongoing geopolitical tensions.

notable_qa.question: Jal Irani (Nuvama) asked for a bifurcation of O2C profit growth drivers.
notable_qa.answer: Management attributed it to a combined effect of petrochemical margins, diesel crack spreads, and the benefit of the TC fleet mitigating freight costs.

notable_qa.question: Sanjay Mookim (J.P. Morgan) asked for an update on New Energy commissioning.
notable_qa.answer: Solar module capacity is 6+ GW (target 20 GW early next year); BESS facility commissioning expected in next calendar half-year.

notable_qa.question: Sachin Salgaonkar (Bank of America) asked about the timeline for retail margin recovery.
notable_qa.answer: Management expects benefits to start accruing in absolute EBITDA from next year as infrastructure investments scale.

risks: Geopolitical instability in the Middle East and Russia impacting crude supply and freight costs.
Intense competition in the online retail/quick commerce space leading to margin pressure.
Inflationary pressures impacting consumer purchasing power and discretionary demand.
Uncertainty regarding Chinese export quotas and structural demand shifts toward EVs.
